messages.subject: Executive Value Creation Brief | Aramex | Regional Growth & Stakeholder Strategy
messages.body:
Dear Mr. Abdulfatah,

I am sharing a strategic value creation brief prepared for Aramex, focused on commercial growth, resilient logistics, regional trade corridors, institutional relationships and customer-led transformation. My current work spans government and regulatory relations, corporate affairs, ESG, strategic partnerships and cross-functional execution in a multinational mining environment.

The attached brief outlines areas where this experience could support country-level growth and external stakeholder alignment. I would welcome a short discussion regarding senior leadership or strategic mandates where my background would add value.

Regards,
Ragunauth Ramsaroop

strategic_brief.title: Strategic Value Creation Brief for Aramex
strategic_brief.executive_summary: Ragunauth Ramsaroop offers a leadership profile aligned with Aramex's agenda across commercial growth, resilient logistics, regional trade corridors, institutional relationships and customer-led transformation. His experience combines government and regulatory relations, corporate affairs, ESG, strategic partnerships, social performance and executive advisory in a multinational mining environment. He works across operations, legal, finance, procurement, HR, security and technical teams, translating external obligations into coordinated execution. For Aramex, his strongest contribution would sit where country growth, government relationships, customer priorities and operational resilience require common governance, rapid issue resolution and executive accountability across internal teams and external partners.
strategic_brief.company_context: Aramex reported strong 2026 revenue growth while continuing its Accelerate28 transformation and maintaining service continuity during regional disruption. Its freight-forwarding performance, alternative routing and sustainability-linked refinancing show how commercial growth, operational resilience and strategic finance increasingly interact. Country-level leadership in the Gulf also depends on customs, transport authorities, customers, airports, free zones, strategic partners and workforce capability. These interfaces create a need for disciplined stakeholder management and fast cross-functional coordination. A leadership model connecting commercial objectives with government relations, risk management and operational execution can help protect continuity, deepen customer confidence and accelerate growth across strategic trade corridors.

opportunities.title: Country stakeholder architecture
opportunities.rationale: Logistics growth depends on customs, transport authorities, free zones, airports, customers and strategic partners. A structured engagement model can reduce friction and improve visibility of decisions and commitments.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I can build stakeholder maps, engagement calendars and escalation routines linking commercial priorities with government interfaces, operating owners and measurable delivery milestones.

opportunities.title: Trade resilience governance
opportunities.rationale: Regional disruptions require rapid routing, customer communication and regulatory coordination across functions. Prepared governance can shorten response times while preserving accountability, service continuity and stakeholder confidence.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I can establish issue registers, decision protocols and cross-functional crisis routines linking commercial, operations, security, legal and external-relations teams around clear actions.

opportunities.title: Strategic partnership growth
opportunities.rationale: New corridors and customer solutions often require partnerships across infrastructure, technology and local market ecosystems. Clear governance improves execution and strengthens the value case for all parties.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I can structure partnership charters, institutional engagement plans and executive reviews that connect customer opportunities to partner responsibilities, government priorities and operating outcomes.

days_0_30: Map priority customers, government interfaces, trade corridors and strategic issues.
days_31_60: Create stakeholder, issue and partnership governance registers.
days_61_90: Launch cross-functional routines for selected growth and resilience priorities.
days_91_180: Embed executive reporting, lessons learned and scalable country practices.

potential_impact: Faster response to logistics and trade disruptions.
background_relevance: Government and regulatory relations in a complex operating environment.
Corporate affairs, strategic partnerships and commercial coordination experience.
Cross-functional work with operations, legal, finance, procurement, security and executive teams.
